steps.title: Separate deformation from material response
steps.explanation: Start with the reference tetrahedron. F records local shape change; measuring it alone supplies no stress, stored energy or equilibrium condition.
steps.observe: J is 1 and Green strain is zero up to roundoff. No force or pressure readout is fabricated.

steps.title: Use rigid rotation as a strain check
steps.explanation: Rotate the undeformed element by 180 degrees. Green strain depends on F-transpose F, which remains the identity for a rigid rotation.
steps.observe: The element changes orientation while J stays 1 and Green strain remains zero up to roundoff. This verifies kinematics, not objective material energy.

steps.title: Distinguish isochoric shape change from rigidity
steps.explanation: Apply shear 0.25 instead. Its determinant is also 1, but its edge lengths and angles change; a constitutive law would need that information to calculate stress.
steps.observe: Green strain norm becomes about 0.179518 and Y-line stretch about 1.03078 while volume stays fixed. Continue to the material and FEM labs for actual force calculations.

audit.finding: The shared geometry adapter could suggest a continuum solve despite prescribing all positions and hiding its strain measure.
audit.change: Provide identity, rigid-rotation and shear checks with explicit missing constitutive response.
audit.remaining: This chapter example is a kinematic bridge. It does not implement the chapter’s proposed objective-energy, singular-value or finite-deformation material extensions.
